source_text: Yoluntas autem Dei est quam Christus et fecit et docuit. humilitas in conuersatione, stabilitas in fide, uerecundia in uerbis, in factis iustitia, in operibus misericordia, in moribus disciplina, iniuriam facere non nosse et factam posse tolerare, cum fratribus pacem tenere, Dominum toto corde diligere, amare in illo quod pater est, timere quod Deus est, Christo nihil omnino . praeponere, quia nec nobis quicquam ille praeposuit, caritati eius inseparabiliter adhaerere, cruci eius fortiter ac fidenter adsistere, quando de eius nomine et honore certamen est, exhibere in sermone constantiam qua confitemur, in quaestione fiduciam qua congredimur, in morte patientiam qua coronamur: hoc est coheredem Christi uelle esse, hoc est praeceptum Dei facere, hoc est uoluntatem patris inplere.
thought_title: The will of God is Christ's humility, faith, love, and endurance
orientation: Cyprian is explaining what doing God's will means, after citing John on not loving the world.
pass_a_gloss: Will [the] but of God is which Christ both did and taught. humility in [way of] life, steadfastness in faith, modesty in words, in deeds justice, in works mercy, in habits discipline, injury to do not to know and [when] done to be able to endure, with [the] brothers peace to hold, [the] Lord with [the] whole heart to love, to love in him that [he] father is, to fear that God is, to Christ nothing at all to prefer, because nor to us anything he preferred, to [the] love of him inseparably to cling, to [the] cross of him bravely and confidently to stand by, when about his name and honor [the] contest is, to show in speech [the] constancy by which we confess, in questioning [the] confidence with which we engage, in death [the] patience by which we are crowned: this is co-heir of Christ to wish to be, this is [the] command of God to do, this is [the] will of [the] Father to fulfill.

choices.term: Yoluntas autem Dei est quam Christus et fecit et docuit
choices.english: But the will of God is what Christ both did and taught
choices.why: Keeps the exact double verb 'did and taught' and the identifying 'is what' structure; 'autem' as 'but' marks the turn from the previous citation.
rejected: Now the will of God is that which Christ both performed and taught

choices.term: iniuriam facere non nosse et factam posse tolerare
choices.english: not knowing how to do injury and being able to endure injury done
choices.why: Preserves the two infinitives with 'non nosse' and 'posse' as parallel abilities, and 'factam' as the injury already done.
rejected: not to know how to inflict wrong and to be able to bear wrong inflicted

choices.term: amare in illo quod pater est, timere quod Deus est
choices.english: to love in him that he is Father, to fear that he is God
choices.why: Keeps the compact 'quod pater est / quod Deus est' clauses and the distinction between love and fear.
rejected: to love him as Father, to fear him as God

choices.term: Christo nihil omnino . praeponere, quia nec nobis quicquam ille praeposuit
choices.english: to prefer nothing at all to Christ, because he also preferred nothing to us
choices.why: Retains the reciprocal 'praeponere' and the emphatic 'nihil omnino' and 'nec...quicquam'.
rejected: to put nothing whatsoever before Christ, since he put nothing before us either

choices.term: hoc est coheredem Christi uelle esse
choices.english: this is to will to be coheir of Christ
choices.why: Keeps 'uelle esse' as 'to will to be' rather than smoothing to 'to want to be', preserving the volitional force.
rejected: this is to want to be a coheir with Christ

pass_b_english: But the will of God is what Christ both did and taught: humility in conduct, steadfastness in faith, restraint in words, justice in deeds, mercy in works, discipline in habits, not knowing how to do injury and being able to endure injury done, keeping peace with brothers and sisters, loving the Lord with the whole heart, loving in him that he is Father, fearing that he is God, preferring nothing at all to Christ, because he also preferred nothing to us, clinging inseparably to his love, standing by his cross bravely and confidently when there is a contest over his name and honor, showing in speech the constancy with which we confess, in trial the confidence with which we engage, in death the patience with which we are crowned. This is to will to be coheir of Christ; this is to do God's command; this is to fulfill the Father's will.
notes: The source has 'Yoluntas' with initial capital Y, likely a manuscript or typographical variant of 'uoluntas'; glossed as 'will'. There is a stray period after 'omnino' in 'Christo nihil omnino . praeponere', possibly indicating a lacuna or punctuation artifact; the gloss treats the phrase as complete.

last_rejected.quote: loving in him that he is Father, fearing that he is God
last_rejected.source_quote: amare in illo quod pater est, timere quod Deus est
last_rejected.why: Latin 'in illo' governs both clauses: 'loving in him that he is Father, fearing in him that he is God'. English drops second 'in him', changing sense.
last_rejected.fix: loving in him that he is Father, fearing in him that he is God
last_rejected.ruling: 'timere quod Deus est' needs no 'in illo'; parallelism is rhetorical. Omission doesn't change meaning.

last_rejected.quote: because he also preferred nothing to us
last_rejected.source_quote: quia nec nobis quicquam ille praeposuit
last_rejected.why: 'praeposuit' means 'put before/prioritized over', not 'preferred to'. Christ put nothing before us, i.e., ranked us first.
last_rejected.fix: because he put nothing before us
last_rejected.ruling: 'praeposuit' = 'preferred'; 'preferred nothing to us' correctly means he ranked us first. Meaning preserved.
